facts.claim: The gut microbiome of people in industrialized populations differs from those living traditional lifestyles, but there were little differences in alpha diversity across lifestyles.
facts.quote: The composition of the gut microbiome in industrialized populations differs from those living traditional lifestyles. ... we found little differences in alpha diversity across lifestyles.

facts.claim: Microbial targeting restored CD4(+) T cell balance and yielded significantly leaner animals regardless of their dietary 'fast food' indiscretions.
facts.quote: Our finding that microbial targeting restored CD4(+) T cell balance and yielded significantly leaner animals regardless of their dietary 'fast food' indiscretions

facts.claim: Ethnic/racial background proved to be one of the strongest associations of both pathways and microbes with clinical metadata.
facts.quote: Metagenomic carriage of metabolic pathways was stable among individuals despite variation in community structure, and ethnic/racial background proved to be one of the strongest associations of both pathways and microbes with clinical metadata.

facts.claim: Changes in agriculture and engineering have altered human eating and living behaviors, which are linked to changes in the bacterial communities within the human body.
facts.quote: Technological advances that have led to changes in agriculture and engineering have altered our eating and living behaviors in ways never before possible in human history. These changes also have altered the bacterial communities within the human body

facts.claim: The abundance of the Western module correlated appropriately with dietary intake of saturated fatty acids, fat-soluble vitamins and fiber in 98 volunteers.
facts.quote: In 98 volunteers the abundance of the Western module correlated appropriately with dietary intake of saturated fatty acids, fat-soluble vitamins and fiber.

facts.claim: The Western module was also coupled to dietary intake in children (and piglets) correlating with formula (vs breast) feeding.
facts.quote: The module was also coupled to dietary intake in children (and piglets) correlating with formula (vs breast) feeding

research.angle: Industrial agriculture and Western diets are linked to distinct shifts in gut microbiome composition and associated health issues, but these changes do not necessarily reduce the overall diversity (alpha diversity) of the microbes.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that industrialization and Western diets significantly reshape the specific types of microbes present in the human gut, but it does not confirm a systematic reduction in overall microbial diversity.
research.caveat: Several studies show that factors like genetics, geography, and ethnicity are also primary drivers of microbiome structure, making it difficult to isolate the impact of the food supply chain alone.
